discovery: Prediction and realization of near-room-temperature superconductivity in compressed hydrogen-rich hydrides
motivation: Ashcroft's old dream that hydrogen-dominant metals should superconduct at very high temperatures has become laboratory reality. Duan and Ma, using first-principles structure searches, predicted specific falsifiable phases: H3S with Tc near 200 K, and the clathrate rare-earth superhydrides such as LaH10 with Tc approaching room temperature. Experiments confirmed both. H3S was observed at 203 K, and Hemley's group, together with independent teams, synthesized LaH10 with Tc around 250-260 K at megabar pressures. Since then the results have been reproduced across many laboratories using resistive, magnetic, spectroscopic and flux-trapping probes. Together this work overturned the long-held belief that conventional phonon-mediated superconductivity cannot exceed roughly 40 K. It established a predictive, theory-led route to discovering new superconductors and opened a new field of extreme-condition quantum matter. Mikhail Eremets, who would surely have shared this recognition, died in 2024.
